primary_claim: An open-source crosscoder trained on Gemma-2 2B base vs. IT models replicates Anthropic's crosscoder model-diffing result: decoder vector norms cluster into shared, base-specific, and chat-specific latent groups, with shared-latent decoder vectors highly aligned between models, and the crosscoder reaches 81 L0, 77% explained variance, and ~95% CE loss recovered.

effect.metric: L0 / explained variance / CE loss recovered
effect.value: L0=81, 77.90%/77.56% explained variance (base/chat), 95.43%/95.67% CE loss recovered (base/chat)

stated_future_work: deep dives on the 'chat-' and 'base-specific' latents to localize key bits of the model that fine-tuning meaningfully changes
more rigorous interpretability analyses of specific interesting latents
limitations_stated: not sure why there is an asymmetry between base-specific (~60) and chat-specific (~225) latent counts
without other public crosscoders as reference points, still developing intuitions for what constitutes strong performance
hyperparameters were selected from intuition and not systematically tuned
only looked at a handful of latents, cherry-picking the most interesting ones
quote: On average, the crosscoder has 81 L0, 77% explained variance, and 95% loss recovered relative to zero ablation on the training distribution.
